title: Divine cult is whatever cannot truly suit a creature, even if the worshiper denies he takes the object for God
source_text: XXII. Itaque ab eo cultu primo removent omnia quae, secundum Scripturae doctrinam, ad divinum cultum pertinent. Ut autem cultus pro divino habeatur non necesse est, ex eorum mente, ut qui illum exhibet, objectum quod colit habeat pro supremo Numine, a quo omnia pendeant, ipsum vero a nullo, & quod sit rerum omnium primum principium & finis ultimus: adeoque cultum suum absolute in eo terminet, nec ad alium ullum superiorem referre intendat. Sed sufficit ut cultus sit talis, qui revera creaturae convenire non possit: propterea quod quiddam divinum in ea supponit; etiamsi aliter per errorem judicet ille a quo cultus ejusmodi defertur.
pass_a_gloss: And so they first remove from that cult everything which, according to the doctrine of Scripture, belongs to the divine cult. But for a cult to be held divine it is not necessary, in their mind, that the one who shows it take the object he cultivates for the supreme Deity, on whom all things depend while he depends on none, and who is the first principle and last end of all things, and so terminate his cult absolutely in it and not intend to refer it to any other superior. It is enough that the cult be such as cannot really suit a creature, because it supposes something divine in it, even if the one by whom such a cult is paid judges otherwise by error.
pass_b_english: Whatever Scripture counts as divine worship is first stripped away from honor of the blessed.
A cult is divine even if the worshiper does not consciously take its object for the supreme God, the first principle and last end.
It is enough that the act cannot really suit a creature, because it assumes something divine in that creature.
The worshiper's mistaken explanation does not change the nature of the act.

choices.english: even if he judges otherwise by error
choices.why: Intention does not reclassify an act that only a divine object can bear.
rejected: only explicit atheism makes a cult divine
